verses.text: The LORD's message came to me:
"Son of man, give the people of Israel a riddle and tell them a story.
Say, 'This is what the Lord GOD says: A great eagle with powerful wings, long feathers, and thick, colorful plumage came to Lebanon. It took hold of the top of a cedar tree.
It broke off the highest branch and carried it to a land of traders, where it planted it in a city of merchants.
Then it took one of the seeds of the land and planted it in fertile soil. It planted it beside plenty of water, like a willow.
The seed sprouted and became a low, spreading vine. Its branches turned toward the eagle, and its roots grew down beneath it. So it became a vine, grew branches, and put out leafy shoots.

But there was another great eagle with powerful wings and thick plumage. Now the vine sent its roots toward this eagle and stretched out its branches to it from the bed where it was planted, hoping the eagle would water it.
Yet it had been planted in good soil beside plenty of water, so that it could grow branches, bear fruit, and become a fine vine.'

Say, 'This is what the Lord GOD says: Will it do well? Won't it be pulled up by its roots and stripped of its fruit, so that all its new leaves wither? It will not take a strong arm or many people to pull it up by its roots.
Even if it is transplanted, will it do well? Won't it wither completely when the east wind hits it? It will wither in the bed where it grew.'"
Then the LORD's message came to me:
"Say to these rebellious people, 'Don't you know what these things mean?' Tell them, 'The king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and took its king and officials back with him to Babylon.
Then he took a member of the royal family and made a treaty with him, putting him under oath. He also took away the leading men of the land,
so that the kingdom would be kept weak and unable to rise again. It could survive only by keeping his treaty.

But the king of Judah rebelled against him by sending messengers to Egypt to get horses and a large army. Will he succeed? Can someone who does such things escape? Can he break the treaty and still escape?
As surely as I live, says the Lord GOD, he will die in Babylon, in the land of the king who put him on the throne, whose oath he despised and whose treaty he broke.
Pharaoh with his mighty army and great crowd of soldiers will not help him in battle, when siege ramps are built and siege walls set up to kill many people.
He despised the oath by breaking the treaty. He gave his hand in a pledge and still did all these things. He will not escape.
So this is what the Lord GOD says: As surely as I live, I will bring down on his head the oath he despised and the covenant he broke, which was made in my name.
I will spread my net over him, and he will be caught in my trap. I will bring him to Babylon and judge him there because he was unfaithful to me.
All the best of his troops will die by the sword, and the survivors will be scattered to every wind. Then you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken.'

This is what the Lord GOD says: 'I myself will take a shoot from the very top of a cedar and plant it. I will break off a tender sprig from its highest branches and plant it on a high and lofty mountain.
I will plant it on the high mountain of Israel. It will grow branches and bear fruit and become a magnificent cedar. Birds of every kind will nest in it and find shelter in the shade of its branches.

All the trees of the field will know that I, the LORD, bring down the tall tree and make the low tree grow tall. I dry up the green tree and make the dry tree flourish. I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will do it.'"
